terms_note: SP-API Developer Agreement; private apps may only serve the developer's own organisation; public apps must list in the Selling Partner Appstore. Connecting guide lists host, x-amz-access-token, x-amz-date and user-agent request headers (no request signing); the runtime sends x-amz-access-token and its own user-agent but no x-amz-date.

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes**.Confidence: **high** — official developer documentation opened by the auditor.
auth: 1. Tenant (Professional seller) registers a developer profile + private app in Developer Central; self-authorises → LWA refresh token; stores client id / secret / refresh token in our channel vault.
2. Client exchanges the refresh token for a 1-hour access token (`refresh_access_token`) and calls SP-API with it.
3. Public-app path (one platform app for all tenants) needs Appstore listing + Amazon review.

endpoints.purpose: create / update / delete listing (productType + attributes payload)

reference.limits: Token bucket per operation and seller-app pair (rate + burst); standard plans documented per operation, dynamic plans auto-adjust per seller; `x-amzn-RateLimit-Limit` header; 429 QuotaExceeded is retryable (client maps to RateLimited, retry 60 s). - SP-API Developer Agreement + Data Protection Policy; private apps serve only the developer's organisation; public apps reviewed and listed in the Appstore. - Professional plan required.
mcp_sdk: SDK: Amazon-generated SDKs with built-in LWA auth (SP-API docs)
SDK: Data Kiosk API for sales + traffic analytics

sandbox.notes: SP-API hosted sandbox: https://sandbox.sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com, -eu and -fe (the region config field fills {region}). The LWA token endpoint is the production one (api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token, unchanged) with the app's normal credentials. The static sandbox answers only requests that match the examples in each API model exactly (other arguments return an error); operations with dynamic-sandbox support return realistic responses. Sandbox rate limit: 5 requests/second, burst 15; restricted operations need a production Restricted Data Token.

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: LWA client identifier of your SP-API application (Developer Central / Solution Provider Portal > app > LWA credentials).

fields.name: client_secret
fields.help: LWA client secret of the same application.

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.help: LWA refresh token (Atzr|...) from self-authorising the app for your seller account (or from the seller's OAuth authorization); exchanged at https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token for 1-hour access tokens sent as x-amz-access-token.

config_fields.name: region
config_fields.help: SP-API endpoint region: na (Canada, US, Mexico, Brazil), eu (Europe, UK, India, Middle East, Turkey, South Africa) or fe (Japan, Australia, Singapore); calls go to https://sellingpartnerapi-<region>.amazon.com.

config_fields.name: seller_id
config_fields.help: Selling partner (merchant token) id used in the Listings Items path /listings/2021-08-01/items/{sellerId}/{sku} (Seller Central > Settings > Account Info > Merchant Token).

config_fields.name: marketplace_id
config_fields.help: Marketplace id the tools act on, e.g. ATVPDKIKX0DER (US) or A1F83G8C2ARO7P (UK); see the SP-API Marketplace IDs page.

config_fields.name: currency
config_fields.help: Currency of the marketplace's offers (e.g. USD, GBP, EUR); needed only when update_listing changes the price (purchasable_offer selector).

me.note: GET /sellers/v1/marketplaceParticipations returns {payload: [{marketplace{id, countryCode, name, defaultCurrencyCode}, participation{isParticipating, hasSuspendedListings}}]} — the marketplaces the seller can sell in.

update_listing.note: PATCH /listings/2021-08-01/items/{sellerId}/{sku}?marketplaceIds (listing_id = your SKU) with productType PRODUCT and two JSON-Patch `merge` operations as in the Manage purchasable offer / Merge a listing guides: /attributes/purchasable_offer [{marketplace_id, currency, audience: ALL, our_price[{schedule[{value_with_tax: price}]}]}] and /attributes/fulfillment_availability [{fulfillment_channel_code: DEFAULT, quantity}]; a merge leaves omitted sub-attributes unchanged. `currency` comes from the config field. `title`/`description` (item_name / product_description need language_tag per marketplace) are not changed. Returns {sku, status ACCEPTED|INVALID|VALID, submissionId, issues[]}; processing is asynchronous.

end_listing.note: DELETE /listings/2021-08-01/items/{sellerId}/{sku}?marketplaceIds deletes the listings item for that marketplace (irreversible; listing_id = your SKU). Returns {sku, status ACCEPTED|INVALID, submissionId, issues[]}.

set_inventory.note: PATCH /listings/2021-08-01/items/{sellerId}/{sku} with a `merge` on /attributes/fulfillment_availability [{fulfillment_channel_code: DEFAULT, quantity}] (Merge a listing guide) sets seller-fulfilled (MFN) quantity without touching restock_date / lead time. `sku` (or listing_id, which is the SKU on Amazon) addresses the listing. FBA stock is Amazon's and cannot be set.

list_orders.note: GET /orders/v0/orders?MarketplaceIds&CreatedAfter(ISO-8601)&OrderStatuses(Pending|Unshipped|PartiallyShipped|Shipped|Canceled|Unfulfillable|...)&MaxResultsPerPage(1-100). `since` is REQUIRED in practice (Amazon: either CreatedAfter or LastUpdatedAfter must be set). Only the first page is returned: Amazon paginates with NextToken (raw payload.NextToken), not page numbers, so `page` > 1 repeats page 1. Rate 0.0167 req/s, burst 20. OrderTotal.Amount is a decimal string. Orders v0 getOrders is marked deprecated in favour of Orders v2026-01-01 searchOrders.

not_offered.create_listing: putListingsItem (PUT /listings/2021-08-01/items/{sellerId}/{sku}) requires {productType, requirements, attributes{...}} where attributes are product-type-specific arrays defined by the Product Type Definitions API (item_name[{value, language_tag, marketplace_id}], condition_type, purchasable_offer, externally_assigned_product_identifier, ...); the vocabulary has no product type and the attribute schema changes per type.
not_offered.mark_shipped: confirmShipment (POST /orders/v0/orders/{orderId}/shipmentConfirmation) requires {marketplaceId, packageDetail{packageReferenceId, carrierCode, trackingNumber, shipDate, orderItems[{orderItemId, quantity}]}} — the orderItemIds come from getOrderItems (GET /orders/v0/orders/{orderId}/orderItems) first, two calls.
not_offered.listing_metrics: Per-listing sales and traffic are only available through asynchronous Reports (createReport, poll getReport, download the document) or Data Kiosk queries — no synchronous metrics call.

evidence: probe: 5/5 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route answered 403 too, so the host authenticates before routing
